scope: Lightweight static and local execution audit; no deployment performed.

checks.finding: Application reads paths relative to repository root for local evidence, but Spark/HDFS host and artifact locations are fixed in code. Local Python/runtime paths also appear in scripts and execution instructions.
Application loads v4 Parquet and Spark ML model from hdfs://localhost:9000 and uses local WebHDFS assumptions. A public host will not have this machine's HDFS volumes.
Flask debug is off and binds to loopback for local use; Flask's built-in development server is used and is explicitly unsuitable for production. No production WSGI/ASGI process configuration exists.

Production secrets are environment-managed, but the local browser verifier contains fixed test-only login credentials. Do not reuse these credentials or expose the local test database; rotate/bootstrap separate credentials for any deployment.

Registration, session auth, password hashing, CSRF, role/location authorization and admin account controls are implemented and locally tested. Production cookie/TLS/secret hardening and a separate evaluator account remain required.

Query filters, prediction inputs, management payloads, export limits, customer-profile privacy and invalid roles are validated. Request-size limits, broad payload fuzzing and production abuse controls are not evidenced.

Unhandled errors return a generic 500 message; startup health preserves degraded status. Stack traces and configuration internals are not sent through the generic route handler. Operational logging/monitoring is incomplete.
No CORS extension is configured for the same-origin local UI. Mutating authenticated API requests require CSRF tokens; allowed origins must be specified if cross-origin use is introduced.
Only Flask==3.1.3 is pinned for the app. There is no complete lock/requirements file for Python, pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, joblib, PySpark, Java, or browser/runtime compatibility.
Application startup requires live HDFS, Spark/PySpark and readable canonical v4 tables/model. Docker Compose only defines Hadoop services, not the web app or Spark serving runtime.
Verified Spark model is loaded once and inference works locally. Model exists in HDFS rather than a deployment-portable artifact; no cloud model delivery/provenance bootstrap is documented.
No versioned local/object-store export package for canonical aggregates or Spark model, no checksums/manifest-driven loader, and no export/import test. Do not point a public host at local HDFS.
DINEIQ_PORT is read by the app, but HDFS namenode/WebHDFS roots, model path and result paths are not configurable. Bind address and operational settings are mostly fixed.

Operational profiles use application-issued anonymous keys and reject direct identifiers in behavior features; role checks are present. Source data still contains identifying fields and a full retention/privacy policy is not documented.

Warm aggregate endpoints are fast. One local forecast response took 4.24 s, close to the SRS five-second target; startup was 10.37 s. No concurrent-load, memory, uptime, or representative production test exists.

Generated CSVs total hundreds of MB, Spark execution logs are several MB each, comparison JSON is about 850 KB, and the Python estimator is about 12 MB. Keep large datasets/HDFS artifacts out of ordinary Git; publish external access or reproducible build instructions.

Durable application audit events, health reporting and truthful historical Spark execution evidence exist. Live job events, production log aggregation, uptime monitoring and alerting are not implemented.

minimal_reproducible_public_serving_path: Keep the verified Spark/HDFS pipeline unchanged.
Export canonical v4 result Parquet (or explicitly derived compact serving files) and the persisted selected model into a versioned artifact bundle from the verified HDFS paths.
Generate a manifest with source canonical paths/version, export time, row counts, schemas, model version, feature contract, and checksums; test export against canonical evidence.
Add configurable artifact root and serving backend selection; do not silently fall back to sample/mock data.
Test a clean deployment-like environment with no Docker HDFS and validate that its bundle is provenance-matched to v4/model v1.

Add a production WSGI server, full pinned dependency lock, health/readiness configuration, production cookie/TLS hardening, separate evaluator credentials, and managed deployment secrets before public hosting.
